pick.headline: Budapest memorandum on Ukraine's nuclear disarmament
pick.summary: On December 5, 1994, at a CSCE summit in Budapest, the United States, Britain and Russia signed memoranda giving security assurances to Ukraine, Belarus and Kazakhstan in return for giving up their Soviet nuclear weapons.
pick.significance: The agreement removed the world's third-largest nuclear arsenal from Ukraine.
pick.fbis: The Central Eurasia Daily Report of December 5, 1994, carried Kiev radio on Kuchma arriving for the Budapest CSCE summit, and Paris AFP: Ukraine signed the NPT in exchange for security guarantees from the US, Russia and Britain.

alternates.headline: Soviet Union and Afghanistan sign a friendship treaty
alternates.summary: On December 5, 1978, Afghan leader Nur Mohammad Taraki and Leonid Brezhnev signed a twenty-year Treaty of Friendship, Good-Neighborliness and Cooperation in Moscow.
alternates.significance: Moscow later cited the treaty as the legal basis for its invasion of Afghanistan a year later.
alternates.fbis: The Soviet Union Daily Report of December 5, 1978, listed, under South Asia, the Taraki-led Afghan delegation's Moscow visit: Kremlin talks begun and ended, and the friendship and cooperation treaty signed.

alternates.headline: Warsaw Pact leaders meet in Moscow on the Polish crisis
alternates.summary: On December 5, 1980, the leaders of the Warsaw Pact states met in Moscow to discuss the crisis in Poland, amid Western fears of a Soviet invasion.
alternates.significance: US intelligence, warned by the CIA's agent in the Polish general staff, Ryszard Kuklinski, judged an intervention possible; President Carter publicly warned Moscow.
alternates.fbis: The Eastern Europe Daily Report of December 8, 1980, opened with Warsaw Pact reportage and comment on the leaders' meeting, and listed Bulgarian and Czechoslovak leaders returning from the Moscow Warsaw Pact meeting.
